subject: Change to tomorrow's small gathering
text:
Due to a last-minute complication, I need to alter the small gathering I had arranged for tomorrow afternoon. The original study room became unavailable this evening, so I have moved the session to the quieter corner of the campus library. I am writing to ask whether you might still be willing to join a friend and me, even though the change comes very late. My intention was only to create a relaxed setting where you could meet a peer who has gone through a similar course, and the new room should still suit that purpose. The table is larger, though the lighting is less flattering, and I hope you will overlook these minor inconveniences.

If the revised timing or location is difficult, please say so without concern. I do not want the adjustment to feel like an imposition, particularly as this is our first interaction. I can also send a brief note outlining where we will be seated or propose another time later this week. My aim is simply to introduce you to someone who may be able to offer useful perspective, and I would be glad if you could still attend. I appreciate your understanding, especially given the sudden change to my original plan. I look forward to hearing from you.
